test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The LCM of the two numbers is 1440 and their HCF is 32. If the first number is 288, then find the second number.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The fundamental property of two numbers is: **Product of Numbers = LCM × HCF**.

Since 1440 is a multiple of 288 (1440 ÷ 288 = 5).

The second number is simply 5 × 32 = 160.

**∴ The correct answer is 160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**LCM** of two numbers = 1440

**HCF** of two numbers = 32

**First Number** (a) = 288

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = **LCM × HCF**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c0d4025e7e500dc65cb1c2bc08629d2dac90efcd54e975a101c749bec7868b1d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 288 × Second Number = 1440 × 32

⇒ Second Number = (1440 × 32) ÷ 288

⇒ Second Number = 46080 ÷ 288

⇒ Second Number = 160

**∴ The correct answer is 160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule

For any two positive integers a and b, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (a × b = HCF × LCM).

HCF and LCM Relationship

The **HCF** of any set of numbers is always a factor of their **LCM**.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime, their **HCF is 1** and their **LCM is the product** of the two numbers.</p
